source_text:
Διὰ πίστιν καὶ φιλοξενίαν ἐσώθη Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη.
ἐκπεμφθέντων γὰρ ὑπὸ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ τοῦ Ναυὴ κατασκόπων εἰς τὴν Ἱεριχώ, ἔγνω ὁ βασιλεὺς τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἥκασιν κατασκοπεῦσαι τὴν χώραν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐξέπεμψεν ἄνδρας τοὺς συλλημψομένους αὐτούς, ὅπως συλλημφθέντες θανατωθῶσιν.
ἡ οὖν φιλόξενος Ῥαὰβ εἰσδεξαμένη αὐτοὺς ἔκρυψεν εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον ὑπὸ τὴν λινοκαλάμην.
ἐπισταθέντων δὲ τῶν παρὰ τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ λεγόντων: Πρὸς σὲ εἰσῆλθον οἱ κατάσκοποι τῆς γῆς ἡμῶν: ἐξάγαγε αὐτούς, ὁ γὰρ βασιλεὺς οὕτως κελεύει, ἥδε ἀπεκρίθη: Εἰσῆλθον μὲν οἱ ἄνδρες, οὓς ζητεῖτε, πρός με, ἀλλ’ εὐθέως ἀπῆλθον καὶ πορεύονται τῇ ὁδῷ: ὑποδεικνύουσα αὐτοῖς ἐναλλάξ.
καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς ἄνδρας: Γινώσκουσα γινώσκω ἐγώ, ὅτι κύριος ὁ θεὸς παραδίδωσιν ὑμῖν τὴν γῆν ταύτην: ὁ γὰρ φόβος καὶ ὁ τρόμος ὑμῶν ἐπέπεσεν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν αὐτήν. ὡς ἐὰν οὖν γένηται λαβεῖν αὐτὴν ὑμᾶς, διασώσατέ με καὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου.
καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῇ: Ἔσται οὕτως, ὡς ἐλάλησας ἡμῖν. ὡς ἐὰν οὖν γνῷς παραγινομένους ἡμᾶς, συνάξεις πάντας τοὺς σοὺς ὑπὸ τὸ στέγος σου, καὶ διασωθήσονται: ὅσοι γὰρ ἐὰν εὑρεθῶσιν ἔξω τῆς οἰκίας, ἀπολοῦνται.
καὶ προσέθεντο αὐτῇ δοῦναι σημεῖον, ὅπως ἐκκρεμάσῃ ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου αὐτῆς κόκκινον, πρόδηλον ποιοῦντες, ὅτι διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ κυρίου λύτρωσις ἔσται πᾶσιν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν καὶ ἐλπίζουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν.
ὁρᾶτε, ἀγαπητοί, ὅτι οὐ μόνον πίστις, ἀλλὰ καὶ προφητεία ἐν τῇ γυναικὶ γέγονεν.
thought_title: Rahab saved by faith and hospitality
orientation: Clement is giving examples from Scripture of faith and hospitality, and has just begun the story of Rahab the prostitute in Jericho.
pass_a_gloss: Through faith and hospitality was saved Rahab the prostitute. [When] had been sent out [the] spies by Joshua the [son] of Nun into Jericho, knew the king of the land that they had come to spy out their country, and he sent out men [who were] to seize them, so that having been seized they might be put to death. The hospitable Rahab, having received them, hid [them] in the upper room under the flax-stalks. [When] stood by the [men] from the king and said: To you entered the spies of our land: bring them out, for the king thus commands, she answered: Entered indeed the men whom you seek to me, but immediately they departed and are going on the road: pointing out to them in the opposite direction. And she said to the men: Knowing I know that the Lord God is delivering to you this land: for the fear and the trembling of you has fallen upon those dwelling in it. When therefore it happens [for] you to take it, save me and the house of my father. And they said to her: It will be so, as you spoke to us. When therefore you know [that] we are arriving, you will gather all your [people] under your roof, and they will be saved: for as many as are found outside the house will perish. And they added to give her a sign, so that she might hang from her house [something] scarlet, making [it] clear beforehand that through the blood of the Lord redemption will be for all those believing and hoping in God. You see, beloved, that not only faith but also prophecy was in the woman.

choices.why: The compound means flax (λινο-) stalks or reeds (καλάμη); 'flax-stalks' keeps the agricultural specificity of what Rahab used to hide the spies.
The adverb means 'crosswise' or 'in the opposite direction'; Rahab deliberately misdirects the pursuers, so the rendering must convey that she pointed them away from the spies' actual route.
The participle phrase means 'making it evident beforehand'; the scarlet sign is a type of Christ's blood, so the forward-pointing sense of πρόδηλον matters.
The noun means ransom-payment or release; 'redemption' is the standard theological term and matches the blood-of-the-Lord typology Clement draws.
The cognate participle plus finite verb is a Hebrew-style intensifying construction; 'I know for certain' carries the emphatic force without awkward repetition.

bible_refs.note: The whole Rahab episode is retold from Joshua 2, including the spies, the flax-stalks, the scarlet cord, and the promise to save her household.

pass_b_english: Rahab the prostitute was saved because of her faith and hospitality.

Joshua son of Nun sent spies into Jericho. The king of the land learned that they had come to spy out his country, so he sent men to seize them, intending to put them to death once they were captured.
But the hospitable Rahab took the spies in and hid them in the upper room under the flax stalks.

When the king's men arrived, they said, 'The spies of our land have come to you. Bring them out, for the king commands it.' She answered, 'The men you are looking for did come to me, but they left at once and are on their way,' while pointing them in the opposite direction.

Then she said to the spies, 'I know for certain that the Lord God is giving you this land, for fear and trembling of you has fallen on all who live in it. So when you take it, save me and my father's household.'
They said to her, 'It will be as you have said. When you learn that we are coming, gather all your people under your roof, and they will be saved. For whoever is found outside the house will perish.'

They also gave her a sign, so that she would hang a scarlet cord from her house. This made it clear in advance that through the blood of the Lord there will be redemption for all who believe and hope in God.
You see, beloved, that not only faith but also prophecy was at work in this woman.

polish.changed: Clarified who is speaking and who each pronoun refers to, especially distinguishing the king's men from the spies and Rahab's words to each. Broke long sentences into shorter, more natural modern English sentences while preserving every claim, quotation, and Scripture reference.
Clarified who is speaking and acting in each scene, smoothed sentence order, and made the sequence of events easier to follow aloud without altering any claims or quotations.

last_rejected.quote: through the blood of the Lord
last_rejected.why: τοῦ κυρίου here refers to the Israelite commander (Joshua/Lord of the army), not to God/Christ; anachronistic christological reading
last_rejected.fix: 'through the blood of the lord [of the army]' or 'through the lord's blood' with context clear
last_rejected.ruling: διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ κυρίου is a standard early Christian typological reading; 'the Lord' is a defensible rendering of τοῦ κυρίου, not a clear mistranslation.
